title: Agricultural Stress Index — Dekadal — Global 1km
description: Agricultural Stress Index (ASI) — Dekadal product. ASI depicts the percentage of arable land within an administrative area that has been affected by drought conditions from the start of the season up to the current dekad. This example illustrates the FAO ISO 19115-1 STAC profile end-to-end: every iso:* field is populated, alongside fao:* identifiers and fields contributed by the standard extensions listed in stac_extensions.

providers.name: FAO-UN-Global Information and Early Warning System (GIEWS)

sci:citation: FAO GIEWS, Agricultural Stress Index (ASI) — Dekadal product. https://example.org/cite/asi-d
iso:lineage_statement: ASI is computed by integrating the Vegetation Health Index (VHI) over time and space using crop phenology and crop mask layers; values below the VHI=35 threshold are accumulated per administrative area to produce the percentage of stressed arable land. For information on ASIS methodology, pre-processed global/country level maps/zonal statistics, raw raster imagery data dissemination channels, ASIS-based research and FAQs etc., please visit FAO GIEWS Earth Observation website at: https://www.fao.org/giews/earthobservation/index.jsp
iso:purpose: FAO Global Information and Early Warning System on Food and Agriculture (GIEWS) monitors the condition of major foodcrops across the globe to assess production prospects. To support the analysis and supplement ground-based information, GIEWS utilizes remote sensing data that can provide a valuable insight on water availability and vegetation health during the cropping seasons. In addition to rainfall estimates and the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), GIEWS and FAO's CBC Division have developed the Agricultural Stress Index (ASI), a quick-look indicator for the early identification of agricultural areas probably affected by dry spells, or drought in extreme cases. The ASIS was online in 2014.

iso:supplemental_information: Indicator values 251-254 are reserved sentinels (off-season, no-data, no-seasonality, no-cropland-or-grassland) and should be excluded from numerical analysis; see classification:classes on the data band for the full sentinel table.

docs-gee.title: ASIS GEE Assets 2026 Migration Note
docs-gee.description: Due to recent FAO backend geospatial infrastructure upgrade, ASIS assets on GEE need to be adjusted accordingly. The main changes involve the naming of the ImageCollection IDs and the Image IDs within each ImageCollection. These changes take effect on 20 January 2026. The update of the old assets has been stopped and the archive will be deleted by the end of March.
